# libcbor / cbor_load_fuzzer

libcbor's own fuzz target `cbor_load_fuzzer` ([source](source/cbor_load_fuzzer.cc), unmodified), one of the targets OSS-Fuzz builds, over libcbor (PJK/libcbor at d436c402).

cbor_load the input; on success cbor_describe to /dev/null, cbor_serialize_alloc (the serialized buffer is freed without being compared to the input or re-loaded), cbor_copy (the copy is never compared to the original), decref both. A 1 GiB cap makes the hooks return NULL (allocation failure, not a check).

## How this program differs from what OSS-Fuzz runs
- Linked against libcbor at commit d436c402.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the harness one to four times and prints each return value.

## What the harness checks
The harness makes no check of its own beyond not crashing. Its halts statements say only that the code it calls never crashes, hangs or trips a sanitizer. Its agreement statements say only that the code never crashes or trips a sanitizer, and allow a run that never ends. Its bound statements say only how often its builds may disagree. Its decidability statements say only that some program decides where its builds agree.

## Builds
Static riscv64 Linux programs, compiled for RV64G and run as `<file> <input-file>`; `oft fetch libcbor` downloads the published ones and checks each against its SHA-256.

| build | file | bytes | sha256 |
|---|---|---:|---|
| plain | `cbor_load_fuzzer.plain` | 296,176 | `942c5fad7f0d40a333c5ec7e5354b6dd32f07d3b2c16580161fc0dfbf1ac6223` |
| ubsan | `cbor_load_fuzzer.ubsan` | 305,016 | `82fa899ea996a04aea5922841615638dc0e2041f44bed7eb2212ac8d04678e98` |
| asan | `cbor_load_fuzzer.asan` | 828,376 | `4e774b895ceaa0c02a3959d012031badc69751ed3c981a7854d5d24bc1537154` |
| asan-ubsan | `cbor_load_fuzzer.asan-ubsan` | 838,744 | `7079bd86fc0c0ef1d1e199b96be34923682a42401929438af0dc21f36c30e538` |

Each build also links code that no sanitizer instruments, as its link recorded it. A statement about a sanitizer build covers that code only as uninstrumented code: ASan checks no load or store made inside it, and UBSan inserts no check there.

- plain: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc++.a` (the C++ runtime), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
- ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc++.a` (the C++ runtime), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
- asan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc++.a` (the C++ runtime), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
- asan-ubsan: `clang_rt.crtbegin.o` (compiler-rt), `libclang_rt.asan.a` (the sanitizer runtime), `libclang_rt.builtins.a` (compiler-rt), `crt1.o` (the C library), `libc++.a` (the C++ runtime), `libc.a` (the C library), `libunwind.a` (the C++ runtime)
